title: Tech Note: Are You V6 Ready?
author: David Adams
featured_technology: EXECUTE statement / STR# resource #8 compatibility mechanism
Stored procedures returning negative process IDs

historical_commentary.text: Published ahead of 4D v6's release, this note prepares developers for breaking changes coming in the new version — renamed core terminology (Files become Tables, Layouts become Forms), a compatibility mechanism for EXECUTE statement source code stored via STR# resource #8, much longer identifier names (31 characters, up from 15/11), a new pointer sign syntax, and stored procedures now returning negative process IDs — all of which describe a one-time historical migration milestone that has long since been completed and superseded by many subsequent major 4D versions.
related_updates: 4D has undergone many major version transitions since v6 (v6->v7->...->v20+), each with its own compatibility and migration considerations documented in later release notes
The specific v6 terminology changes (Tables/Forms) described here have long since become simply the standard, familiar 4D vocabulary
Modern 4D's compiler and language have evolved substantially further (Project Mode, ORDA, modern object/collection types) beyond anything anticipated in this 1996 pre-release note
